# Read me

This paper aims to understand human-vulture perception of conflict regarding the role of the Andean Condor (*Vultur gryphus*) as a potential predator. The specific aims were: 

* To examine local perceptions of the negative impacts of condors as potential predator of livestock, and analyze how these perceptions relate to socio-demographic and psychological factors, livestock management practices, and experience or attitude by farmers.

* To examine local perceptions of the condor's contributions to farmers: negative due to perception of harmfulness, positive due to perceived benefits and values, or a combination of both, and analyze how these perceptions relate to socio-demographic and psychological factors, livestock management practices, and experience or attitude by farmers (including perception of attacking livestock).

* To assess whether field observations support the reported perceptions of condor-related damage

* To explore how people's perceptions of the costs and benefits associated with condors, and the previous exposure to environmental workshops, influence coexistence-based conservation behaviors (evaluate conservation behaviors).

A further work will assess attitudes (feelings, disappear, population preference change) as response variables, but in this study we focused on perceptions as response variables.

## Useful functions

```{r}
# Predict from parameters
predict_from_params <- function(params, newdata, model) {
  # number of beta coefficients
  nb <- length(model$coefficients)
  
  # replace coefficients
  model$coefficients <- params[1:nb]
  
  # replace thresholds
  model$zeta <- params[(nb+1):length(params)]
  
  predict(model, newdata, type = "probs")
}

# Predicting from multinomial parameters
predict_multinom_params <- function(par, newdata, model) {
  
  # number of non-reference categories and predictors
  K <- length(model$lev) - 1
  P <- length(model$coefnames)
  
  # reshape parameter vector into matrix
  par_mat <- matrix(par, nrow = K, ncol = P, byrow = TRUE)
  rownames(par_mat) <- model$lev[-1] # all but the reference
  colnames(par_mat) <- model$coefnames
  
  # extract RHS of formula (no response)
  rhs <- delete.response(terms(model))
  
  # model matrix for newdata
  X <- model.matrix(rhs, newdata)
  
  # linear predictors for each non-reference category
  eta <- X %*% t(par_mat)   # dim: [rows × K]
  
  # add reference category (0)
  eta_full <- cbind(0, eta)
  
  # softmax to convert to probabilities
  probs <- exp(eta_full) / rowSums(exp(eta_full))
  
  colnames(probs) <- model$lev
  
  return(probs)
}

# Inverted logit to convert linear predictors to probabilities
invlogit <- function(x) exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))

# AICc comparison for Firth's bias-reduced logistic regression
AICc_logistf <- function(model) {
  ll <- model$loglik  # penalized log-likelihood (implemented in logistf)
  K  <- length(model$coef)  # number of parameters
  n  <- model$n  # sample size
  
  AIC  <- -2 * ll + 2 * K # AIC formula
  AICc <- AIC + (2 * K * (K + 1)) / (n - K - 1) # small sample correction
  
  return(data.frame(AIC = AIC, AICc = AICc, K = K))
}

# Make predictions from logistic regression with penalized likelihood
make_pred_df <- function(model, newdata, xvar) {
  
  pred_lp <- predict(model, newdata, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  
  newdata$lp      <- pred_lp$fit
  newdata$lp_low  <- pred_lp$fit - 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit
  newdata$lp_high <- pred_lp$fit + 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit
  
  invlogit <- function(x) exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
  
  newdata$pred      <- invlogit(newdata$lp)
  newdata$pred_low  <- invlogit(newdata$lp_low)
  newdata$pred_high <- invlogit(newdata$lp_high)
  
  newdata$xvar <- newdata[[xvar]]
  
  return(newdata)
}
```

```{r Geographic and demographic exploratory}
FigSite <- perceptions |>
  mutate(Site = ifelse(`Paddock site` == 0, "Antisana", "Llanganates")) |>
  ggplot(aes(x = Site)) +
```

# Perception of people that Andean condor attacks livestock (aim 1)

Farmers perceive the Andean condor as a livestock predator, but vary with socio-demographic, farm characteristics, and experience/attitudes

## Perception of attack predicted by socio-demographic (1a)

This is an ordinal variable (gradually ascending from Never to Often)
```{r}
perceptions_Y1 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(perceptions_1 = ordered(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?`, 
                          levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3)),
         site = as.factor(ifelse(`Paddock site` == 0, "Antisana",
                       "Llanganates")),
         gender = as.factor(ifelse(Gender == 0, "Male", "Female")),
         age = Age,
         edu.level = factor(`Education level`, 
                       levels = 0:4, 
                       labels = c("0-None","1-Prim","2-High","3-Tech","4-Univ")),
         t.residence = `Time of residence`,
         occupation = as.factor(ifelse(Occupation == 0, "Employer","Owner")))

# sequencial contrast for education level
contrasts(perceptions_Y1$edu.level) <- MASS::contr.sdif(5)

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_perceptions_demogra <- list(
  site  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ site,  data = perceptions_Y1),
  gender  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ gender,  data = perceptions_Y1),
  age   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ age,  data = perceptions_Y1),
  edu.level  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ edu.level,  data = perceptions_Y1),
  t.residence  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ t.residence,  data = perceptions_Y1),
  occupation   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ occupation,  data = perceptions_Y1)
  )

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_perceptions_demogra) # edu.level and t.residence

mods_perceptions_demogra <- list(
  null = polr(perceptions_1 ~ 1,
              data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  site  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ site,
               data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  gender  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ gender,
                 data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  age   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ age, 
               data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  edu.level  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ edu.level, 
                    data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  t.residence  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ t.residence, 
                      data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  occupation   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ occupation, 
                      data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  # after first single model with deltaAIC < 2 for two models: edu.level and t.residence
  edu.t.res = polr(perceptions_1 ~ edu.level + t.residence,
                   data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE),
  global = polr(perceptions_1 ~ edu.level + t.residence + age + gender + site + occupation,
                   data = perceptions_Y1, Hess = TRUE)
)

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_perceptions_demogra) # edu.level and t.residence
```

Getting the p-value for the predictors in the model

```{r}
ctbl_m1 <- coef(summary(mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res))
pvals_m1 <- pnorm(abs(ctbl_m1[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
ctbl_m1 <- cbind(ctbl_m1, "p value" = pvals_m1)
ctbl_m1
```

This identify that passing from primary to high school (second contrast, p = 0.0074) and Time of residence (p = 0.026) are the most significant predictors.

```{r}
exp(coef(mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res)[2]) # estimated coefficient for Education level - Primary to High school
exp(coef(mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res)[5]) # estimated coefficient for Time of residence
```

Moving from Primary to High school education increases by 5 times the odds of perceiving condors as harmful. Each additional year of residence increases the odds of perceiving condors as harmful by about 2.8%.

We can extract the coefficients and the variance-covariance to simulate probabilities with new data for the two variables
```{r}
nsim = 1000

# extract coefficients and vcov
coefs.ed.tr <- c(coef(mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res), # slope
                 mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res$zeta) # thresholds
vc.ed.tr <- vcov(mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res)
vc.safe <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(vc.ed.tr)$mat)

# simulate parameter sets
sim_coefs <- mvrnorm(nsim, mu = coefs.ed.tr, Sigma = vc.safe)
```

Generate new data for education level and median time of residence
```{r}
newdat_ed <- expand.grid(
  edu.level = levels(perceptions_Y1$edu.level),
  t.residence = median(perceptions_Y1$t.residence)
)
```

And new data for timer of residence range, including the levels of education level
```{r}
newdat_tr <- expand.grid(
  edu.level = levels(perceptions_Y1$edu.level),
  t.residence = seq(min(perceptions_Y1$t.residence),
                    max(perceptions_Y1$t.residence),
                    length = 100)
)
```

And predict probabilities for each simulation
```{r}
pred_list_ed <- lapply(1:nsim, function(i) {
  predict_from_params(sim_coefs[i,], newdat_ed, mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res)
})

pred_array_ed <- simplify2array(pred_list_ed)
# dim: [ row, category, simulation ] = 5 (as in newdat_ed) x 4 ordinal outcomes (Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often) x 1000 simulations

# summarizing and CI across simualtions
med_ed <- apply(pred_array_ed, c(1, 2), median)
low_ed <- apply(pred_array_ed, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.025)
upp_ed <- apply(pred_array_ed, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

# dim: [ row, category ] = 5 x 4
 
colnames(med_ed) <- c(paste("med_ed",colnames(med_ed)))
colnames(low_ed) <- c(paste("low_ed",colnames(low_ed)))
colnames(upp_ed) <- c(paste("upp_ed",colnames(upp_ed)))

pred_ed <- cbind(newdat_ed, med_ed, low_ed, upp_ed)

# convert to long format
pred_ed_long <- pred_ed |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("med_ed", "low_ed", "upp_ed")),
    names_to = c("stat", "cat"),
    names_pattern = "(med_ed|low_ed|upp_ed) (\\d)",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(Category = recode(cat,
                      "0" = "Never",
                      "1" = "Rarely",
                      "2" = "Sometimes",
                      "3" = "Often"),
         Category = factor(Category,
                              levels = c("Never", 
                                         "Rarely", 
                                         "Sometimes", 
                                         "Often"))) |>
  dplyr::select(-cat) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,
    values_from = value,
    names_prefix = ""
  ) |>
  rename(
    median = `med_ed`,
    lower  = `low_ed`,
    upper  = `upp_ed`
  )

# Time of residency

pred_list_tr <- lapply(1:nsim, function(i) {
  predict_from_params(sim_coefs[i,], newdat_tr, mods_perceptions_demogra$edu.t.res)
})

pred_array_tr <- simplify2array(pred_list_tr)
# dim: [ row, category, simulation ] = 500 (as in newdat_tr) x 4 ordinal outcomes (Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often) x 1000 simulations

# summarizing and CI across simualtions
med_tr <- apply(pred_array_tr, c(1, 2), median)
low_tr <- apply(pred_array_tr, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.025)
upp_tr <- apply(pred_array_tr, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

# dim: [ row, category ] = 500 x 4
 
colnames(med_tr) <- c(paste("med_tr",colnames(med_tr)))
colnames(low_tr) <- c(paste("low_tr",colnames(low_tr)))
colnames(upp_tr) <- c(paste("upp_tr",colnames(upp_tr)))

pred_tr <- cbind(newdat_tr, med_tr, low_tr, upp_tr)

# convert to long format
pred_tr_long <- pred_tr |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("med_tr", "low_tr", "upp_tr")),
    names_to = c("stat", "cat"),
    names_pattern = "(med_tr|low_tr|upp_tr) (\\d)",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(Category = recode(cat,
                      "0" = "Never",
                      "1" = "Rarely",
                      "2" = "Sometimes",
                      "3" = "Often"),
         Category = factor(Category,
                              levels = c("Never", 
                                         "Rarely", 
                                         "Sometimes", 
                                         "Often"))) |>
  dplyr::select(-cat) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,
    values_from = value,
    names_prefix = ""
  ) |>
  rename(
    median = `med_tr`,
    lower  = `low_tr`,
    upper  = `upp_tr`
  )
```

And make the figures
```{r}
p_ed_ci <- ggplot(pred_ed_long, aes(x = edu.level, 
                         y = median, 
                         color = Category)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper), position = position_dodge(width = 0.5))+
  geom_vline(xintercept = 2.5, linetype = "dashed", color = "gray")+

                     limits = c(0,1))+

       y = "Perception of condors attacking livestock", 
       tag = "a)")+

        axis.text.x = element_text(angle = 25, hjust = 1, vjust = 1))
p_ed_ci

p_tr_ci <- ggplot(pred_tr_long,
                  aes(x = t.residence,
                      y = median)) +
  stat_summary(fun.data = function(z) data.frame(
    y = median(z),
    ymin = quantile(z, 0.25),
    ymax = quantile(z, 0.75)
  ), geom = "ribbon", alpha = 0.1, color = NA, aes(fill = Category)) +
  stat_summary(fun = median, geom = "line", size = 1.2, aes(color = Category)) +

  scale_y_continuous(expand = c(0,0),
                     limits = c(0,1))+
  scale_x_continuous(expand = c(0,0),

p_tr_ci
```

![**Perpection of attacts perceived by socio-economics.** Two socio-economic variables more clearly related with the predicted probability of perceibing condors attacking livestock (model selected with AICc). This probability is ordered by the ordinal perception of condors attacking livestock Never, Rarely, Sometimes, and Often (colors). Variation represents 95% confidence intervals as a measure of uncertainty after 1000 simulation of the parameters.](figs/Fig_Aim1_a_perception.jpg)

## Perception of attack predicted by farm characteristics (1b)

Same ordinal variable (gradually ascending from Never to Often)
```{r}
perceptions_Y2 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(perceptions_1 = ordered(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?`, 
                          levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3)),
         t.livestock = ifelse(`Type of livestock`== 0, "0-Cattle",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==1, "1-Horse",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==2,"2-Cattle and horse",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==3, "3-Cattle, horse, and sheep",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==4, "4-Cattel, horse, and lama",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==5, "5-Cattle and lama",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==6, "6-All",
                       NA))))))),
         n.cattle = ifelse(is.na(Cattle), 0, Cattle),
         n.horses = ifelse(is.na(Horse), 0, Horse),
         n.sheep = ifelse(is.na(Sheep), 0, Sheep),
         n.lama = ifelse(is.na(Lama), 0, Lama),
         t.production = ifelse(`Type of cattle production`== 0, "0-Beef",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==1, "1-Dairy",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==2,"2-Brave",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==3, "3-Beef, dairy, and brave",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==4, "4-Beef and dairy",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==5, "5-Dairy and brave",
                                    NA)))))))

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_perceptions_farm <- list(
  null = polr(perceptions_1 ~ 1, data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  t.livestock  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ t.livestock,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  n.cattle  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.cattle,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  n.horses   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.horses,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  n.sheep  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.sheep,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  n.lama  = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.lama,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  # as farmers include combination of livestock, we can include these additive potential effects
  n.cattle.horse = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.cattle + n.horses,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  n.cattle.lama = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.cattle + n.lama,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  t.production   = polr(perceptions_1 ~ t.production,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  global = polr(perceptions_1 ~ t.livestock + n.cattle + n.horses + n.lama + n.sheep + t.production,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE),
  global.2 = polr(perceptions_1 ~ n.cattle + n.horses + n.lama + n.sheep + t.production,  data = perceptions_Y2, Hess = TRUE)
  )

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_perceptions_farm) # all but t.livestock... cattle?
```

Getting the p-value for the predictors in the model

```{r}
ctbl_m2 <- coef(summary(mods_perceptions_farm$n.cattle))
pvals_m2 <- pnorm(abs(ctbl_m2[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
ctbl_m2 <- cbind(ctbl_m2, "p value" = pvals_m2)
ctbl_m2
```

This indicates that although the number of lamas is the best model, that relationship with perception is not clear

```{r}
exp(coef(mods_perceptions_farm$n.cattle)[1]) # estimated coefficient for number of cattle
```

Each individual up in number of lamas multiplies the odds of consider the condor harmful by ~1.00569 (0.5%).

Plot the results with a new dataset for predictions
```{r}

)

upp_m2 <- apply(pred_array_m2, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

# dim: [ row, category ] = 100 x 4
```

We can combine this figure with the next sub aim

## Perception of attack predicted by experiences/attitudes (1c)

Same ordinal variable (gradually ascending from Never to Often)
```{r}
perceptions_Y3 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(perceptions_1 = ordered(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?`, 
                          levels = c(0, 1, 2, 3)),
         seen.attack = ifelse(`Have you ever seen condors attacking living livestock?` == 0, "1-Yes",
                       "0-No"),
         perc.popcha = ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 0, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 1, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 2, "1-Remains stable",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 3, "2-Increased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 4, "2-Increased",
                       NA))))),
         atti.feeling = ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 0, "4-Like a lot",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 1, "3-Like",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 2, "2-Indifferent",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 3, "1-Dislike",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 4, "0-Dislike a lot",
                       NA))))),
         atti.dissap = ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 0, "0-Very happy",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 1, "1-Happy",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 2, "2-Indifferent",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 3, "3-Sad",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 4, "4-Very sad",
                       NA))))),
         atti.popcha = ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 0, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 1, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 2, "1-Remains stable",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 3, "2-Increased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 4, "2-Increased",
                       NA))))),
    # reorder binomial (0 = No, 1 = Yes)
    workshop = ifelse(`Have you attended talks/trainings on the environment?` == 0, 1, 0)
         )

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_perceptions_expatt <- list(
  null = polr(perceptions_1 ~ 1, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  seen.attack = polr(perceptions_1 ~ seen.attack, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  perc.popcha = polr(perceptions_1 ~ perc.popcha, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  atti.feeling = polr(perceptions_1 ~ atti.feeling, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  atti.dissap = polr(perceptions_1 ~ atti.dissap, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  atti.popcha = polr(perceptions_1 ~ atti.popcha, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  workshop = polr(perceptions_1 ~ workshop, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE),
  global = polr(perceptions_1 ~ seen.attack + perc.popcha + atti.feeling + atti.dissap + atti.popcha + workshop, data = perceptions_Y3, Hess = TRUE)
    )

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_perceptions_expatt) # seen.attack and null
```

Getting the p-value for the predictors in the model

```{r}
ctbl_m3 <- coef(summary(mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack))
pvals_m3 <- pnorm(abs(ctbl_m3[, "t value"]), lower.tail = FALSE) * 2
ctbl_m3 <- cbind(ctbl_m3, "p value" = pvals_m3)
ctbl_m3
```

This indicates that although have seen an attack is the best model, that relationship with perception is not clear

```{r}
exp(coef(mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack)[1]) # estimated coefficient for number of lamas
```

Have seen an attack by condor multiplies the odds of consider the condor harmful by 2 times.

Plot the results with a new dataset for predictions
```{r}
newdat_m3 <- expand.grid(
  seen.attack = levels(as.factor(perceptions_Y3$seen.attack))
)

# simulate data
nsim = 1000

# extract coefficients and vcov
coefs.m3 <- c(coef(mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack), # slope
                 mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack$zeta) # thresholds
vc.m3 <- vcov(mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack)
vc.safe.m3 <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(vc.m3)$mat)

# simulate parameter sets
sim_coefs.m3 <- mvrnorm(nsim, mu = coefs.m3, Sigma = vc.safe.m3)

# predict values from model
pred_list_m3 <- lapply(1:nsim, function(i) {
  predict_from_params(sim_coefs.m3[i,], newdat_m3, mods_perceptions_expatt$seen.attack)
})

pred_array_m3 <- simplify2array(pred_list_m3)
# dim: [ row, category, simulation ] = 100 (as in newdat_m2) x 4 ordinal outcomes (Never, Rarely, Sometimes, Often) x 1000 simulations

# summarizing and CI across simualtions
med_m3 <- apply(pred_array_m3, c(1, 2), median)
low_m3 <- apply(pred_array_m3, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.025)
upp_m3 <- apply(pred_array_m3, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

# dim: [ row, category ] = 100 x 4
 
colnames(med_m3) <- c(paste("med_m3",colnames(med_m3)))
colnames(low_m3) <- c(paste("low_m3",colnames(low_m3)))
colnames(upp_m3) <- c(paste("upp_m3",colnames(upp_m3)))

pred_m3 <- cbind(newdat_m3, med_m3, low_m3, upp_m3)

# convert to long format
pred_m3_long <- pred_m3 |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("med_m3", "low_m3", "upp_m3")),
    names_to = c("stat", "cat"),
    names_pattern = "(med_m3|low_m3|upp_m3) (\\d)",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  mutate(Category = recode(cat,
                      "0" = "Never",

  dplyr::select(-cat) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,

  ) |>

    median = `med_m3`,

  )

p_seen <- ggplot(pred_m3_long, aes(x = seen.attack,
```

# Perception of harmfulness or mixed compared to beneficial (aim 2)

Farmers perceive the Andean condor as beneficial, harmfulness, or a combination (mixed perception). However, these perceptions vary with socio-demographic, farm characteristics, and experience/attitudes

## Perception of harmfulness or mixed compared to beneficial predicted by socio-demographic (2a)
This is a nominal outcome, without an specific order (Beneficial, Harmful, Both)

```{r}
perceptions_Y4 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(Y_benefit = ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 0, "Harmful",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 1, "Beneficial",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 2, "Both",
                            NA))),
         Y_benefit = factor(Y_benefit, 
                            levels = c("Beneficial",
                                       "Harmful",
                                       "Both")),
         site = as.factor(ifelse(`Paddock site` == 0, "Antisana",
                       "Llanganates")),
         gender = as.factor(ifelse(Gender == 0, "Male", "Female")),
         age = Age,
         edu.level = factor(`Education level`, 
                       levels = 0:4, 
                       labels = c("0-None","1-Prim","2-High","3-Tech","4-Univ")),
         t.residence = `Time of residence`,
         occupation = as.factor(ifelse(Occupation == 0, "Employer","Owner")))

# sequencial contrast for education level
contrasts(perceptions_Y4$edu.level) <- MASS::contr.sdif(5)

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_benefit_demogra <- list(
  null =  multinom(Y_benefit ~ 1,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  site  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ site,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  gender  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ gender,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  age   = multinom(Y_benefit ~ age,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  edu.level  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ edu.level,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  t.residence  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ t.residence,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  occupation   = multinom(Y_benefit ~ occupation,  data = perceptions_Y4),
  global = multinom(Y_benefit ~ site + gender + age + edu.level + t.residence + occupation, data = perceptions_Y4), 
  # after two models within deltaAICc < 2
  site.tres = multinom(Y_benefit ~ site + t.residence, data = perceptions_Y4),
  site.tres.int = multinom(Y_benefit ~ site + t.residence + site*t.residence, data = perceptions_Y4)
  )

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_benefit_demogra) # site, t.residence, and null; when adding

summary(mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)
```

To get the p-values
```{r}
z_benef <- summary(mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)$coefficients / summary(mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)$standard.errors
pvals_benef <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_benef)))
pvals_benef
```

Our research question for the model was "What socio-demographic factor makes farmers perceive condors as harmful or both harmful and beneficial, instead of only beneficial?" Farmers who have lived longer in the area are more likely to report a mixed perception (both beneficial and harmful) compared to beneficial. Although farmers in Llanganates tend to be more likely to perceive the condor as harmful than beneficial, the uncertainty is too large and not statistically supported.

Plot the results with a new dataset for predictions
```{r}
newdat_m4 <- expand.grid(
  site = levels(as.factor(perceptions_Y4$site)),
  t.residence = seq(min(perceptions_Y4$t.residence),
                    max(perceptions_Y4$t.residence),
                    length = 100)
)

# simulate data
nsim = 1000

# extract coefficients and vcov
coefs.m4 <- as.vector(t(coef(mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)))
vc.m4 <- vcov(mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)
vc.safe.m4 <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(vc.m4)$mat)

# simulate parameter sets

# predict values from model
pred_list_m4 <- lapply(1:nsim, function(i) {
  predict_multinom_params(sim_coefs.m4[i,], newdat_m4, mods_benefit_demogra$site.tres)
})

pred_array_m4 <- simplify2array(pred_list_m4)
# dim: [ row, category, simulation ] = 200 (as in newdat_m4) x 3 levels (Beneficial, Both, harmful) x 1000 simulations

# summarizing and CI across simualtions

low_m4 <- apply(pred_array_m4, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.025)
upp_m4 <- apply(pred_array_m4, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

# dim: [ row, category ] = 200 x 3
 
colnames(med_m4) <- c(paste("med_m4",colnames(med_m4)))
colnames(low_m4) <- c(paste("low_m4",colnames(low_m4)))
colnames(upp_m4) <- c(paste("upp_m4",colnames(upp_m4)))

pred_m4 <- cbind(newdat_m4, med_m4, low_m4, upp_m4)

# convert to long format
pred_m4_long <- pred_m4 |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("med_m4", "low_m4", "upp_m4")),
    names_to = c("stat", "Category"),
    names_pattern = "(med_m4|low_m4|upp_m4) (.*)",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,
    values_from = value
  ) |>
  rename(
    median = med_m4,
    lower  = low_m4,
    upper  = upp_m4
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Category = factor(Category,
                      levels = c("Beneficial", "Harmful", "Both"))
  )

# visually representing the results of the model

  "Beneficial" = "dashed",

  "Both"       = "solid"
)

       aes(x = t.residence, y = median)) +

per_m4
```

## Perception of harmfulness or mixed compared to beneficial predicted by farm characteristics (2b)
This is a nominal outcome, without an specific order (Beneficial, Harmful, Both)

```{r}
perceptions_Y5 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(Y_benefit = ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 0, "Harmful",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 1, "Beneficial",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 2, "Both",
                            NA))),
         Y_benefit = factor(Y_benefit, 
                            levels = c("Beneficial",
                                       "Harmful",
                                       "Both")),
         t.livestock = factor(ifelse(`Type of livestock`== 0, "0-Cattle",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==1, "1-Other",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==2,"1-Other",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==3, "1-Other",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==4, "1-Other",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==5, "1-Other",
                       ifelse(`Type of livestock`==6, "1-Other",
                       NA)))))))),
         n.cattle = ifelse(is.na(Cattle), 0, Cattle),
         n.horses = ifelse(is.na(Horse), 0, Horse),
         n.sheep = ifelse(is.na(Sheep), 0, Sheep),
         n.lama = ifelse(is.na(Lama), 0, Lama),
         t.production = factor(ifelse(`Type of cattle production`== 0, "0-Beef",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==1, "1-Dairy",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==2,"2-Brave",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==3, "3-Multiple",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==4, "3-Multiple",
                                    ifelse(`Type of cattle production`==5, "3-Multiple",
                                    NA))))))))

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_benefit_farm <- list(
  null =  multinom(Y_benefit ~ 1,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  t.livestock  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ t.livestock,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.cattle  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.cattle,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.horses   = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.horses,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.sheep  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.sheep,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.lama  = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.lama,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  # as farmers include combination of livestock, we can include these additive potential effects
  n.cattle.horse = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.cattle + n.horses,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.cattle.horse.sheep = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.cattle + n.horses + n.sheep,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  n.cattle.lama = multinom(Y_benefit ~ n.cattle + n.lama,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  t.production   = multinom(Y_benefit ~ t.production,  data = perceptions_Y5),
  global = multinom(Y_benefit ~ t.livestock+n.cattle+n.horses+ t.production,  
                    data = perceptions_Y5)
  )

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_benefit_farm) # n.cattle.horse, n. horses, n. sheeps

summary(mods_benefit_farm$n.horses)
```

To get the p-values
```{r}
z_benef_farm <- summary(mods_benefit_farm$n.horses)$coefficients / summary(mods_benefit_farm$n.horses)$standard.errors
pvals_benef_farm <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_benef_farm)))
pvals_benef_farm
```

Our research question for the model was "What farm characteristic predictor makes farmers perceive condors as harmful or both harmful and beneficial, instead of only beneficial?" Many models are equally possible. For simplicity, we can pickup the number of horses, which had the highest weight.

## Perception of harmfulness or mixed compared to beneficial predicted by experiences/attitudes (2c)
This is a nominal outcome, without an specific order (Beneficial, Harmful, Both)

```{r}
perceptions_Y6 <- perceptions |>
  mutate(Y_benefit = ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 0, "Harmful",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 1, "Beneficial",
                     ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 2, "Both",
                            NA))),
         Y_benefit = factor(Y_benefit, 
                            levels = c("Beneficial",
                                       "Harmful",
                                       "Both")),
         seen.attack = ifelse(`Have you ever seen condors attacking living livestock?` == 0, "1-Yes",
                       "0-No"),
         perc.popcha = ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 0, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 1, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 2, "1-Remains stable",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 3, "2-Increased",
                       ifelse(`Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`== 4, "2-Increased",
                       NA))))),
         atti.feeling = ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 0, "4-Like a lot",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 1, "3-Like",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 2, "2-Indifferent",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 3, "1-Dislike",
                       ifelse(`What are your feelings towards Andean condors?`== 4, "0-Dislike a lot",
                       NA))))),
         atti.dissap = ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 0, "0-Very happy",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 1, "1-Happy",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 2, "2-Indifferent",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 3, "3-Sad",
                       ifelse(`What would you feel if all of the condors disappeared forever from the region?`== 4, "4-Very sad",
                       NA))))),
         atti.popcha = ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 0, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 1, "0-Decreased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 2, "1-Remains stable",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 3, "2-Increased",
                       ifelse(`Would you like the Andean condor population in the National Park and the surrounding area to?`== 4, "2-Increased",
                       NA))))),
         perc.attack = ifelse(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?` == 0, "0-Never",
                           ifelse(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?` == 1, "1-Rarely",
                           ifelse(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?` == 2, "2-Sometimes",
                           ifelse(`Do you think condors attack living livestock?` == 3, "3-Often",NA)))),
         # reorder binomial (0 = No, 1 = Yes)
    workshop = ifelse(`Have you attended talks/trainings on the environment?` == 0, 1, 0)
         )

# a list of ordered logistic regression
mods_benefit_att <- list(
  null =  multinom(Y_benefit ~ 1,  data = perceptions_Y6),
  seen.attack = multinom(Y_benefit ~ seen.attack, data = perceptions_Y6),
  perc.popcha = multinom(Y_benefit ~ perc.popcha, data = perceptions_Y6),
  atti.feeling = multinom(Y_benefit ~ atti.feeling, data = perceptions_Y6),
  atti.dissap = multinom(Y_benefit ~ atti.dissap, data = perceptions_Y6),
  atti.popcha = multinom(Y_benefit ~ atti.popcha, data = perceptions_Y6),
  perc.attack = multinom(Y_benefit ~ perc.attack, data = perceptions_Y6),
  workshop = multinom(Y_benefit ~ workshop, data = perceptions_Y6),
  global = multinom(Y_benefit ~ seen.attack + perc.popcha + atti.feeling + atti.dissap + atti.popcha + perc.attack + workshop, data = perceptions_Y6)

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_benefit_att) # perc.attack

summary(mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)
```

To get the p-values
```{r}
z_benef_att <- summary(mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)$coefficients / summary(mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)$standard.errors
pvals_benef_att <- 2 * (1 - pnorm(abs(z_benef_att)))
pvals_benef_att
```

Our research question for the model was "What experience/attitude predictor makes farmers perceive condors as harmful or both harmful and beneficial, instead of only beneficial?" Farmers who think condors attack livestock more often are not more likely to say condors are harmful or have a mixed perception. 

Plot the results with a new dataset for predictions using the covariate.
```{r}
newdat_m6 <- expand.grid(
  perc.attack= levels(factor(perceptions_Y6$perc.attack))
  )

# simulate data
nsim = 1000

# extract coefficients and vcov
coefs.m6 <- as.vector(t(coef(mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)))
vc.m6 <- vcov(mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)
vc.safe.m6 <- as.matrix(Matrix::nearPD(vc.m6)$mat)

# simulate parameter sets
sim_coefs.m6 <- mvrnorm(nsim, mu = coefs.m6, Sigma = vc.safe.m6)

# predict values from model
pred_list_m6 <- lapply(1:nsim, function(i) {
  predict_multinom_params(sim_coefs.m6[i,], newdat_m6, mods_benefit_att$perc.attack)
})

pred_array_m6 <- simplify2array(pred_list_m6)

# summarizing and CI across simualtions
med_m6 <- apply(pred_array_m6, c(1, 2), median)
low_m6 <- apply(pred_array_m6, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.025)
upp_m6 <- apply(pred_array_m6, c(1, 2), quantile, 0.975)

colnames(med_m6) <- c(paste("med_m6",colnames(med_m6)))
colnames(low_m6) <- c(paste("low_m6",colnames(low_m6)))
colnames(upp_m6) <- c(paste("upp_m6",colnames(upp_m6)))

pred_m6 <- cbind(newdat_m6, med_m6, low_m6, upp_m6)

# convert to long format
pred_m6_long <- pred_m6 |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = starts_with(c("med_m6", "low_m6", "upp_m6")),
    names_to = c("stat", "Category"),
    names_pattern = "(med_m6|low_m6|upp_m6) (.*)",
    values_to = "value"
  ) |>
  pivot_wider(
    names_from = stat,
    values_from = value
  ) |>
  rename(
    median = med_m6,
    lower  = low_m6,
    upper  = upp_m6
  ) |>
  mutate(
    Category = factor(Category,
                      levels = c("Beneficial", "Harmful", "Both"))
  )


per_m6 <- ggplot(pred_m6_long,
       aes(x = perc.attack, y = median)) +
  geom_pointrange(aes(ymin = lower, ymax = upper, color = Category), 
                  position = position_dodge(width = 0.5))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1), expand = c(0,0)) +
  scale_color_manual(values = met.brewer("Java"))+
  scale_fill_manual(values = met.brewer("Java"))+
  labs(x = "Perception of condors attacking livestock",
       y = "Perception of condors benefit",
       tag = "c)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
per_m6
```

Combine the figures

```{r}
(per_m4 | per_m5 | per_m6) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
  theme(
    legend.position = "bottom",
    legend.direction = "vertical"
  )
ggsave(filename = "figs/Fig_Aim2_a_b_c_perception.jpg", dpi = 300, 
       width = 360, height = 100, units = "mm")
```
![**Perception of condors benefits for socio-demographic, farm characteristics, and experiences or attitudes vary little.** The probability of perceived condors as beneficial, harmful, or both varied little across different factors (models selected with AICc), regardless of socio-demographics (a), farm characteristics (b; see log scale, only for visualization purposes), or experiences (c). Variation represents 95% confidence intervals as a measure of uncertainty after 1000 simulation of the parameters.](figs/Fig_Aim2_a_b_c_perception.jpg)



# Coexistence behaviors (aim 3)

Participation in environmental workshops and the recognition of beneficial ecosystem services (scavenging) drive the adoption of coexistence-based behaviors.

Here, there are two important behaviors: "leaving carcasses in the field to be consumed by condors" and "educating others about the importance of condor conservation" (Binary outcomes: Logistic regression). The predictors for these behaviors could be "perceived contributions" (beneficial, harmful, both), "attendance at workshops" (yes, no), and "perceptions of population change" (decreased a lot, decreased, remains the same, increased, increased a lot).

```{r warning=FALSE}
perceptions_coex <- perceptions |>
  mutate(
    # reorder binomial (0 = No, 1= yes)
    leave = ifelse(`Do you leave livestock carcasses in the field to be consumed by condors?` == 0, 1, 0),
    # reorder binomial (0 = No, 1= yes)
    educate = ifelse(`Do you educate others about the importance of Andean condor conservation?` == 0, 1, 0),
    # reorder as in previous analysis (0 = beneficial, 1 = harmful, 2 = both)
    perception = ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 1, 0,
                 ifelse(`Could you indicate if the Andean condor is beneficial and/or harmful to you?` == 2, 2, 1)),
    pop.status = `Do you consider that the Andean condor population in this area?`,
    # reorder binomial (0 = No, 1 = Yes)
    workshop = ifelse(`Have you attended talks/trainings on the environment?` == 0, 1, 0))

perceptions_long <- perceptions_coex %>%
  dplyr::select(leave, educate, 
                perception, workshop, pop.status) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(leave, educate), 
               names_to = "Variable", 
               values_to = "Value") 

# exploratory plots
ggplot(perceptions_long, aes(x = Value, y = leave)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, fill = "steelblue", shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth()+
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Probability of leaving carcass") +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,1))

ggplot(perceptions_long, aes(x = Value, y = educate)) +
  geom_point(alpha = 0.2, fill = "firebrick", shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth()+
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Value", y = "Probability of educating others") +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,1))
```

And model selection. First for leaving carcasses
```{r}
mods_leave <- list(
  null       = logistf(leave ~ 1, data = perceptions_coex),
  perception = logistf(leave ~ perception, data = perceptions_coex),
  workshop   = logistf(leave ~ workshop, data = perceptions_coex),
  popstatus  = logistf(leave ~ pop.status, data = perceptions_coex),
  percep2    = logistf(leave ~ perception + I(perception^2), data = perceptions_coex),
  pop2       = logistf(leave ~ pop.status + I(pop.status^2), data = perceptions_coex),
  global     = logistf(leave ~ perception + I(perception^2) + workshop + pop.status + I(pop.status^2), data = perceptions_coex)
)

aic_table_leave <- lapply(mods_leave, AICc_logistf)
aic_table_leave <- do.call(rbind, aic_table_leave)
aic_table_leave <- aic_table_leave |>
  mutate(dAICc = AICc - min(AICc)) |>
  arrange(dAICc)
aic_table_leave
```

and for educating others
```{r}
mods_educate <- list(
  null       = logistf(educate ~ 1, data = perceptions_coex),
  perception = logistf(educate ~ perception, data = perceptions_coex),
  workshop   = logistf(educate ~ workshop, data = perceptions_coex),
  popstatus  = logistf(educate ~ pop.status, data = perceptions_coex),
  percep2    = logistf(educate ~ perception + I(perception^2), data = perceptions_coex),
  pop2       = logistf(educate ~ pop.status + I(pop.status^2), data = perceptions_coex),
  global     = logistf(educate ~ perception + I(perception^2) + workshop + pop.status + I(pop.status^2), data = perceptions_coex)
)

aic_table_educa <- lapply(mods_educate, AICc_logistf)
aic_table_educa <- do.call(rbind, aic_table_educa)
aic_table_educa <- aic_table_educa |>
  mutate(dAICc = AICc - min(AICc)) |>
  arrange(dAICc)
aic_table_educa
```

The behavior of leaving carcass for the condors is weakly related with any hypothesized predictor. The threshold of $\Delta\text{AICc}≤2$ shows that many models, including a "global", are equal possible. We can see the coefficients for these models, showing the marginal increasing trend with perception.

```{r}
aic_table_leave
summary(mods_leave$perception) # marginal increasing trend
summary(mods_leave$pop2) # no effect
summary(mods_leave$percep2) # no effect
summary(mods_leave$global) # none of the variables predict leaving carcasses
```

In contrast, the probability of educating others about the importance of Andean condor conservation clearly increases for farmers that have attended talks/training workshops on conservation. 

```{r}
aic_table_educa
summary(mods_educate$global) # among the variables in global, workshop is the predictor with better relationship
summary(mods_educate$workshop) # the simplified model for workshop confirm this strong relationship
```
Workshop attendance is the dominant predictor of those evaluated. Other predictors add only small improvements (in the global)

# Field observations of condor attacking livestock (aim 4)

Field observations will reveal little evidence of condor predation on live livestock. As such, perceived impacts are likely to exceed those supported by empirical evidence ([Duriez *et al.* 2019](doi:10.1017/S0959270918000345), [Ballejo *et al.* 2020](https://doi.org/10.1016/j.biocon.2020.108627)).

The response variable is an multinomial ordinal (discrete categorical) of ascending severity scale:

```{r}
table(interactions$Interactions)
```

Although this type of data could be analyzed with ordinal regression, providing better results than with traditional count-based models (Poisson, Negative Binomial, Zero-Inflated Poisson, or Zero-Inflated Negative Binomial; see [Valle *et al.* 2019](https://www.nature.com/articles/s41598-019-39377-x)), the small sample size and sparseness of the data make the model to no converge (preliminary analyses not showed). We can group in a binomial response (presence/absence of interaction event), but identifying the "severity" of the interaction with colors in the figure. Let's explore the potential responses.

```{r warning=FALSE}
interactions$Interactions_f <- factor(
  interactions$Interactions,
  levels = c(0,1,2,3),
  labels = c("No", "Light", "Moderate", "Severe")
)

interactions <- interactions |>
  mutate(Interactions_b = case_when(Interactions == 0 ~ 0,
                                    Interactions > 0 ~ 1))

interactions_long <- interactions %>%
  dplyr::select(Interactions_f, Interactions_b, 
                N_Cattle, N_Horses, N_Sheeps, N_Lamas, N_deers, N_Condors) %>%
  pivot_longer(-c(Interactions_b, Interactions_f), 
               names_to = "Variable", 
               values_to = "Value") |>
  mutate(Variable = sub("*._","",Variable))

ggplot(interactions_long, aes(x = Value, y = as.integer(Interactions_b))) +
  geom_jitter(aes(fill = Interactions_f), height = 0.005, alpha = 0.6, color = "steelblue", shape = 21) +
  geom_smooth()+
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_x") +
  labs(x = "Number of animals", y = "Interaction event", fill = "Severity") +
  theme_classic() +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(0,1))
```

This LOESS trend by default in `ggplot` might help us to identify the potential models, discarding the number of lamas and sheeps. Nonetheless, we can compare the different models with AICc.

```{r}
mods_int_log <- list(
  null = glm(Interactions_b ~ 1, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  cattle = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Cattle, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  condors = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Condors, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  deers = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_deers, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  horses = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Horses, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  lamas = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Lamas, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  sheeps = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Sheeps, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  # quadratic of cattle, deers, horses
  cattle.2 = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Cattle + I(N_Cattle^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  deers.2 = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_deers + I(N_deers^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  horses.2 = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Horses + I(N_Horses^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  global = glm(Interactions_b ~ N_Condors + N_deers + I(N_deers^2) + N_Cattle + I(N_Cattle^2) + N_Horses + I(N_Horses^2), data = interactions, family = binomial)
)

AICcmodavg::aictab(mods_int_log) # Condors and deers quadratic

summary(mods_int_log$condors) # clear relationship
summary(mods_int_log$deers.2) # trend
```

As only 4 interaction events have been reported (out of 50; 46 no interactions), the coefficients, p-values, and uncertainty estimates from `glm()` could be unreliable. In addition, the global model reported a LL = 0, a red flag for separation and convergence. Due to these, we can try a Firth's bias-reduced penalized-likelihood logistic regression.

```{r}
mods_int_logistf <- list(
  null = logistf(Interactions_b ~ 1, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  cattle = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Cattle, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  condors = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Condors, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  deers = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_deers, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  horses = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Horses, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  lamas = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Lamas, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  sheeps = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Sheeps, data = interactions, family = binomial),
  # quadratic of cattle, deers, horses
  cattle.2 = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Cattle + I(N_Cattle^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  deers.2 = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_deers + I(N_deers^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  horses.2 = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Horses + I(N_Horses^2), data = interactions, family = binomial),
  global = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_Condors + N_deers + N_Cattle + N_Horses + N_Sheeps + N_Lamas, data = interactions, family = binomial)
)

aic_table_int <- lapply(mods_int_logistf, AICc_logistf)
aic_table_int <- do.call(rbind, aic_table_int)
aic_table_int <- aic_table_int |>
  mutate(dAICc = AICc - min(AICc)) |>
  arrange(dAICc)
aic_table_int # global

summary(mods_int_logistf$global)
```

The negative coefficient for the intercept (and CI also negative) indicate that at value 0 for all predictors (no condors, no livestock), there is no interaction. This is anchoring the model in a starting meaningful way for the covariates (although biologically unrealistic). In mathematical form:

$$
\text{logit}(\alpha) = \beta_0 + \beta_i X_i \cdots  
$$
\noindent where $\alpha$ is the probability of an event to occur (interaction or no interaction), $\beta_0$ the intercept, while $\beta_i$ and $X_i$ are the slope and value for each covariate $i$, respectively. When all $X_i = 0$,
$$
\beta_0 = \log \left( \frac{\alpha}{1-\alpha} \right); \\
$$

\noindent and with an intercept $\approx -6.04$:
$$
\alpha = \frac{e^{-6.04}}{1+e^{-6.04}} \approx 0.002
$$

This indicates that when all the predictors have a count of 0 individuals, the predicted probability of an interaction is $0.2\%$ (this teeny tiny probability is biologically unrealistic, but mathematically useful to understand the effect of the other covariates).  

The clearest relationship of the probability of occurring an interaction event is with the number of condors. Specifically, $\exp(1.063) \approx 2.89$, which means that each additional condor multiplies the odds of an interaction by almost 3 times.

```{r}
newdat_int <- data.frame(
  N_Condors = seq(min(interactions$N_Condors),
                  max(interactions$N_Condors),
                  length = 100),
  N_deers = median(interactions$N_deers),
  N_Cattle = median(interactions$N_Cattle),
  N_Horses = median(interactions$N_Horses),
  N_Sheeps = median(interactions$N_Sheeps),
  N_Lamas = median(interactions$N_Lamas)
)

# linear predictors and standar error for 95% CI
pred_lp <- predict(mods_int_logistf$global, newdat_int, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
newdat_int$lp      <- pred_lp$fit
newdat_int$lp_low  <- pred_lp$fit - 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit
newdat_int$lp_high <- pred_lp$fit + 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit

# Convert to probabilities
newdat_int$pred      <- invlogit(newdat_int$lp)
newdat_int$pred_low  <- invlogit(newdat_int$lp_low)
newdat_int$pred_high <- invlogit(newdat_int$lp_high)


int_a <- ggplot(newdat_int, aes(x = N_Condors, y = pred)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pred_low, ymax = pred_high),
              fill = "firebrick", alpha = 0.15)+
  geom_line(size = 1.2, color = "firebrick") +
  geom_point(data = interactions |>
                dplyr::select(N_Condors,Interactions_b,Interactions_f),
             aes(y = Interactions_b, fill = Interactions_f), 
             alpha = 0.6, shape = 21)+
  scale_fill_manual(values = met.brewer("OKeeffe1",n=3))+
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1))+
  scale_x_continuous(breaks = seq(0,6,1))+
  labs(x = "Number of total condors flying",
       y = "Probability of interaction",
       fill = "Severity",
       tag = "a)") +
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
int_a
```

Now we can include the demographics of the number of condors to see which class is driving the effect of Interactions ~ N_condors. 

```{r}
# a list of models with penalized likelihood
mods_condor_classes <- list(
  null  = logistf(Interactions_b ~ 1,  data = interactions),
  juvF  = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_juviCondorsFeme,  data = interactions),
  subF  = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_subadCondorsFeme, data = interactions),
  adF   = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_adultCondorsFeme, data = interactions),
  juvM  = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_juviCondorsMale,  data = interactions),
  subM  = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_subadCondorsMale, data = interactions),
  adM   = logistf(Interactions_b ~ N_adultCondorsMale, data = interactions)
)

# estimate AICc for penalized likelihood
AICc_logistf <- function(model) {
  ll <- model$loglik  # penalized log-likelihood (implemented in logistf)
  K  <- length(model$coef)  # number of parameters
  n  <- model$n  # sample size
  
  AIC  <- -2 * ll + 2 * K # AIC formula
  AICc <- AIC + (2 * K * (K + 1)) / (n - K - 1) # small sample correction
  
  return(data.frame(AIC = AIC, AICc = AICc, K = K))
}

# construct AIC table
aic_table_condors <- lapply(mods_condor_classes, AICc_logistf)
aic_table_condors <- do.call(rbind, aic_table_condors)
aic_table_condors <- aic_table_condors |>
  mutate(dAICc = AICc - min(AICc)) |>
  arrange(dAICc)
aic_table_condors
```

Two models are identified as the better among these demographics classes: Number of flying juvenile female condors and number of adult male flying condors.

```{r}
mod_juvF <- mods_condor_classes$juvF
mod_adM  <- mods_condor_classes$adM

newdat_juvF <- data.frame(
  N_juviCondorsFeme = seq(min(interactions$N_juviCondorsFeme),
                          max(interactions$N_juviCondorsFeme),
                          length = 100)
  )

newdat_adM <- data.frame(
  N_adultCondorsMale = seq(min(interactions$N_adultCondorsMale),
                           max(interactions$N_adultCondorsMale),
                           length = 100)
)

make_pred_df <- function(model, newdata, xvar) {
  
  pred_lp <- predict(model, newdata, type = "link", se.fit = TRUE)
  
  newdata$lp      <- pred_lp$fit
  newdata$lp_low  <- pred_lp$fit - 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit
  newdata$lp_high <- pred_lp$fit + 1.96 * pred_lp$se.fit
  
  invlogit <- function(x) exp(x) / (1 + exp(x))
  
  newdata$pred      <- invlogit(newdata$lp)
  newdata$pred_low  <- invlogit(newdata$lp_low)
  newdata$pred_high <- invlogit(newdata$lp_high)
  
  newdata$xvar <- newdata[[xvar]]
  
  return(newdata)
}

pred_juvF <- make_pred_df(mod_juvF, newdat_juvF, "N_juviCondorsFeme")
pred_adM  <- make_pred_df(mod_adM,  newdat_adM,  "N_adultCondorsMale")

int_b <- ggplot(pred_juvF, aes(x = xvar, y = pred)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pred_low, ymax = pred_high),
              fill = "steelblue", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2, color = "steelblue") +
  geom_point(data = interactions,
             aes(x = N_juviCondorsFeme, y = Interactions_b, fill = Interactions_f),
             alpha = 0.6, shape = 21) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = met.brewer("OKeeffe1",n=3))+
  labs(x = "Number of juvenile female condors",
       y = "Probability of interaction",
       fill = "Severity",
       tag = "b)") +
  theme_classic()+
  theme(legend.position = "none")
int_b

int_c <- ggplot(pred_adM, aes(x = xvar, y = pred)) +
  geom_ribbon(aes(ymin = pred_low, ymax = pred_high),
              fill = "darkgreen", alpha = 0.15) +
  geom_line(size = 1.2, color = "darkgreen") +
  geom_point(data = interactions,
             aes(x = N_adultCondorsMale, y = Interactions_b, fill = Interactions_f),
             alpha = 0.6, shape = 21) +
  scale_y_continuous(limits = c(0,1)) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = met.brewer("OKeeffe1",n=3))+
  labs(x = "Number of adult male condors",
       y = "Probability of interaction",
       fill = "Severity",
       tag = "c)") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
int_c
```

And combine the figure

```{r}
(int_a / int_b / int_c) +
  plot_layout(guides = "collect") +
```
